anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: The paper describes MNE-BIDS, a standard for organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format, making it a general technical specification/methodology, not a paper about this specific dataset.

anchors.paper_title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
anchors.reason: The paper proposes MEG-BIDS, a general data structure extension for MEG data, which is topically related to neuroimaging but does not describe or introduce the specific dataset on003703.

metadata.methods_description: Data were collected using magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recording techniques with frequency tagging paradigms to investigate syntactic and lexical processing. The dataset is organized according to BIDS standards for electrophysiological data.

funding.award_title: International Laboratory for Social Neuroscience of the Institute for Cognitive Neuroscience HSE

citation_details.title: Syntax Tagging
citation_details.author: Evgenii Kalenkovich
citation_details.abstract: A study of lexical vs. syntactic contributions in cortical tracking of hierarchical linguistic structures. This project contains: - All the code used in the project is in the `git_repository_snapshot` component. - A subset of the code and some of the derived files necessary to recreate the manuscript in the `manuscript_files_repo` and the `manuscript_files_bids` components. The instructions to recreate the manuscript are in the `manuscript_files_repo/README.md`. The MEG data (both raw and the derivatives) are available at https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds003703
